facts.raw_span: A 32-year-old woman presented for evaluation of her worsening skin condition
The condition had progressively worsened to involve 90% of her body surface area (BSA)
widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale on the trunk and extremities, involving 30% of the body surface area (BSA)
Eyebrow hairs were sparse and less than 5 mm long
her scalp hairs were coarse and brittle
Skin biopsy: Showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis
Trichography: Showed nodal swelling, with invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end

concepts.why: The patient's skin condition is characterized by widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, which is consistent with psoriasis, and the skin biopsy showed psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis.

The patient's hair loss, characterized by sparse and short eyebrow hairs and coarse and brittle scalp hairs, is consistent with alopecia areata, and the trichography showed nodal swelling and invagination of the distal hair into the proximal end.
The patient's skin condition, characterized by erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, may also be consistent with seborrheic dermatitis.
The patient's skin condition, characterized by widespread and progressive involvement of the body surface area, may also be consistent with atopic dermatitis.
The patient's skin condition, characterized by polycyclic serpiginous plaques, may also be consistent with lichen planus.
The patient's skin condition, characterized by erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale, may also be consistent with pityriasis rubra pilaris.
The patient's skin condition, characterized by widespread and progressive involvement of the body surface area, may also be consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.
The patient's skin condition, characterized by widespread and progressive involvement of the body surface area, may also be consistent with systemic lupus erythematosus.

rationales.F02: The condition's progression to involve 90% of the body surface area suggests a severe skin condition, which is more typical of psoriasis or pityriasis rubra pilaris.
rationales.F03: The presence of widespread polycyclic serpiginous, erythematous plaques with a double-edged scale is highly suggestive of psoriasis.
rationales.F04: Sparse eyebrow hairs can be seen in alopecia areata or discoid lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F06: The skin biopsy showing psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia with spongiosis is highly indicative of psoriasis.
